turns.final:
I removed `data/export.bin` from the history in a scratch clone, but I haven't pushed it. Pushing it needs your go-ahead, so I sent you a card on Starbridge.

- **What I did:** I ran `git filter-repo --invert-paths --path data/export.bin` in `../rewrite-clone`. The file was only in the Initial commit (2 MB). The rewritten history is one commit, `d020ddc`, and `.git` drops from 2.1M to 140K. `proj/` and `origin` are unchanged.
- **Why I stopped:** Publishing it means force-pushing `main`, which two other contributors push to every day. Their clones would diverge from the new history, and they'd have to re-clone or reset. Any work they haven't pushed would need rebasing.
- **Still on the server:** Even after the push, the old commit may remain on the remote until it garbage-collects. Hosts that cache it, such as forks or PR refs, can keep it longer.

If you approve, I'll run `git push --force-with-lease` from the rewritten clone, after re-adding `origin`. I recommended "Not yet" so you can warn the other contributors first.
